name: Royal jelly
summary: Royal jelly is the milky secretion worker bees feed to queen larvae, sold as a health tonic. This page lists what people say royal jelly does; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose. No ancient writer we could find names royal jelly, so there is no Then and now section; that does not prove it was never used.
inIt: A review of honeybee products says royal jelly holds antimicrobial peptides (jelleins and royalisin), major royal jelly proteins and hydroxy-decenoic acids, notably 10-hydroxy-2-decenoic acid (10-HDA).
Its make-up varies with the bee and the plants around the hive. The UK food table has no royal jelly entry.
processing: Royal jelly spoils easily in storage and processing: a review names protein denaturation, Maillard reactions, enzyme loss and fat oxidation, and says common quality checks (basic chemistry and 10-HDA) do not capture its freshness.

whoShouldBeCareful.with: Asthma, hay fever or other allergies, and bee venom allergy
whoShouldBeCareful.note: In a report of seven people, royal jelly caused asthma and in some cases anaphylaxis after it was swallowed, and IgE antibodies to royal jelly proteins were found in 52% of 75 people with inhalant or food allergies and in 38% of sera from people allergic to bee venom. If you have asthma or allergies, talk to your doctor before using it.

unknowns: Whether royal jelly helps any health problem in people: this page does not review the studies.
How much 10-HDA or protein a given product holds after storage.
Ancient writers: no passage naming royal jelly and the body was found in the open translations that were checked; it is not presented here as an ancient remedy.
